parole.testo: Borrowed from a Slavic language, perhaps from South Slavic, from Ancient Greek σεῦκλον (seûklon). Compare Serbo-Croatian cvekla or Slovak cvikla.

parole.significato: stave (a slightly bent wooden board that forms the sides and bottom of a larger wooden vessel (e.g. barrel, tub, vat))
parole.testo: Borrowed from Slavic, perhaps from South Slavic. Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *dǫga. Compare Bulgarian дъга (dăga, “arc; stave; rainbow”), Serbo-Croatian ду́га /dúga (“stave; rainbow”), Slovene doga (“stave”), Slovak dúha (“stave; rainbow”). First attested in 1233.
Borrowed from a Slavic language (probably from South Slavic). Compare Serbo-Croatian grč.
Borrowed from a Slavic (probably from a South Slavic) language. Compare Bulgarian поп (pop), Serbo-Croatian pop, Russian поп (pop).
Borrowed from a Slavic language (probably from South Slavic), from Proto-Slavic *pečatь. First attested after 1416. The sense stain was first attested in 1791.

parole.significato: true bindweed (any plant of the genus Convolvulus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Slavic (probably South Slavic) language, from Proto-Slavic *sъvolkъ (compare Serbo-Croatian сла̑к /slȃk (“bindweed”), Slovene slak (“bindweed”), Czech svlak (“bindweed”) (dialectal), Bulgarian съвлак (săvlak, “bindweed”) (dialectal)).
